get.description: Read-only WebSocket preview of the session's current owned tab. Requires browse (steer implies browse), since JPEG pixels cannot be redacted. JPEG quality 40, at most 720x450 and 2 fps delivery; capture has a bounded startup allowance of at most 3 frames, then sustained 2 fps. Client messages are ignored and limited to 1 KiB. Secret-tainted tabs are withheld; takeover pauses the preview and takes priority. At most one frame admitted before a safety transition may finish sending within the 5-second writer deadline; later captured frames are excluded. Private sessions return 409 private_session; at most 8 viewers per session (429 too_many_viewers). Device revocation ends its sockets; committed stop/deletion ends existing viewers even if the session immediately resumes. Origin and browser bearer subprotocol rules match takeover.

get.description: WebSocket upgrade for a pending takeover ticket whose target has a tab_id. The daemon streams JPEG frames of that tab (TakeoverServerMessage, JSON text) and forwards TakeoverInput messages to that tab only, with coordinates in viewport CSS pixels. One controller per ticket (409 takeover_in_use); an Origin header must match the Host. Browsers, which cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket, send the token as `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: openside.v1, openside.bearer.<token>`; the daemon answers with `openside.v1` only. The stream ends with an `ended` message on done/reject/expiry, idle timeout, token revocation or tab loss. While the ticket is pending, agent browser tools on the tab are refused with takeover_active.

post.description: Drop the decrypted vault from daemon memory; vault tools stop working until it is unlocked again. Audited (`lock`) after locking, attributed to the caller; 500 vault_locked_audit_incomplete means it is locked but unrecorded. Output masking of values seen while unlocked stays in place until the daemon restarts.

Create the vault file. Keyring backends take no body passphrase and keep a random wrapping key in the OS keyring; a passphrase vault needs `passphrase` (8+ characters), which is never stored or returned. Every attempt that reaches the vault is audited (`setup`: `completed` or `failed` with the code), attributed to the caller (`device:<id>` or `local`). 400 passphrase_required, passphrase_not_used, weak_passphrase; 409 vault_already_set_up; 500 vault_set_up_audit_incomplete (set up and unlocked); 503 keyring_unavailable, vault_unsupported.

Decrypt the vault: a keyring vault re-reads its key from the OS keyring; a passphrase vault needs `passphrase`. Already unlocked is a no-op. Audited (`unlock`: `unlocked`, `denied` with wrong_passphrase, or `failed` with the code), attributed to the caller; an unlock whose record cannot be written does not happen (500 audit_unavailable). Each caller gets 5 wrong passphrases, then waits 30 s, doubling per further wrong one up to 15 min; a success resets it. Paired devices together get 20 wrong passphrases per 15 minutes; the Unix socket is exempt from that shared limit. At most one attempt per caller, and two across paired devices, run at once. Throttled attempts get 429 too_many_attempts with `Retry-After` seconds, before any key derivation, and are not audited. 400 passphrase_required, passphrase_not_used, wrong_passphrase; 409 vault_not_set_up; 503 keyring_unavailable, vault_unsupported.

429.description: Too many wrong passphrases; retry after the `Retry-After` header's seconds
